questions: Do you remain fully conscious and aware during the movements?
Can you stop the movements temporarily when asked or when you concentrate?
Do you feel an urge or inner discomfort that is relieved by making the movements?
Do the movements continue while you are asleep?
Did they start within the past few days?
Are the movements present on both sides of your body?
Do the movements occur in a regular, rhythmic pattern?
Have you had any episodes of staring, loss of awareness, or unresponsiveness?
Have you bitten your tongue or lost bladder control during an episode?
Do you have new weakness, numbness, facial drooping, trouble speaking, or difficulty walking?
Have you had a recent fever, severe headache, head injury, or infection?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medication?
Are you taking medication for psychosis, nausea, epilepsy, depression, or Parkinson’s disease?
Have you used alcohol or recreational drugs recently, or suddenly stopped heavy alcohol use?
Have you previously had similar movements or a seizure?
Does anyone in your family have similar involuntary movements or a neurological disorder?
results: 1. speed of onset: chorea was the INITIAL manifestation of the stroke in 57% of the series; two patients within 24 hours, three between days 2 and 5
2. blood glucose: normal - non-ketotic hyperglycaemia was an exclusion criterion for this series
3. CT head (non-contrast): ischaemic stroke - 92.9% of the series were ischaemic and one was haemorrhagic
4. brain MRI with contrast: lesions in the LENTIFORM NUCLEUS (50%), insula (35.7%), caudate (14.3%) and thalamus (14.3%); cortical in 35.7%, deep in 35.7%, both in 28.6%
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acute unilateral hemichorea/hemiballismus caused by a contralateral ischemic basal-ganglia stroke, most likely involving the lentiform nucleus.

Alternative 1: Hemorrhagic basal-ganglia stroke causing hemichorea/hemiballismus.

Alternative 2: Focal motor seizure with impaired awareness.

Alternative 3: Nonketotic hyperglycemia–associated hemichorea/hemiballismus.
